articleTitle: Optimization Design of Coated Armature in Electromagnetic Railgun Based on Multi-objective Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The electromagnetic railgun is an advanced launch device that accelerates the armature to ultra-high speed through electromagnetic force. The contact between the armature and the two rails is a kind of ultimate sliding electrical contact beyond high pulse current, high speed, and high contact pressure. It leads to excessive local electromagnetic field distribution at the contact interface, which is not conducive to launch performance. In this paper, armatures of different coated structures are considered to improve the electromagnetic field distribution. First, the characteristic-difference scheme based on the bilinear interpolation method is presented to solve the electromagnetic governing equation of the railgun when launching armatures of different coated structures. Second, an optimization design based on NSGA-II is constructed to obtain the Pareto optimal solution set, and an optimized armature of coated structure that brilliantly meets the design objectives is selected. Finally, numerical calculations are conducted based on the optimized parameters to verify the effectiveness of the multimaterial coated armature structure. Results show that the maximum current density of the optimized armature is reduced by 54% compared to the uncoated armature, current diffusion time at the contact interface along the x-direction is shortened by 80 μs, and the penetration depth of the current along the ydirection at the armature-rail contact interface is increased by 1.6 mm, which significantly optimizes the current distribution during the launch process of the electromagnetic railgun.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Solid-State Pulse-Power Generators for High-Voltage Nanosecond Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Pulse power generators are used in a variety of applications ranging from food and water treatment to medical applications. Different circuit topologies and architectures have been proposed to generate short transient pulses. This work compares the performance of four common topologies under similar specifications. In particular, solid-state-based Marx circuit, forward converter-based pulse transformer circuit, the pulse forming network and the capacitor diode voltage multiplier circuit are compared and discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Self-Excitation Characteristics of an Air-Core Brushless Induction Pulsed Alternator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This paper proposes a new type of an air-core brushless induction pulsed alternator (AIPA) that can avoid brush and rotor problems at high speeds. Based on the state space theory, through the position change of the dominant pole of the system, the influence of system parameters (especially the extremely weak magnetizing inductance caused by the air-core structure) on the self-excitation characteristics is analyzed, and basic design principles are given. Finally, the correctness of the theory was verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Development of a prototype Marx generator module for a klystron power-supply in J-PARC linear accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In order to upgrade the acceleration current of the J-PARC linear accelerator, a Marx generator-type klystron power supply is being developed. A prototype of the main Marx module that makes up the power supply and the compensator Marx module that corrects the voltage droop have been manufactured and their performance evaluated.

articleTitle: Constant Magnetic Field Effects on EMRGs: Mechanisms and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: As a high-speed projectile, the electromagnetic railgun has unique application prospects in propulsion technology. Superconducting technology is widely used in business, and it can generate a high-flux constant magnetic field. This study explores the influence of an external constant magnetic field on the thrust and muzzle arc of the electromagnetic railgun. Through simulation analysis, the influence of the superposition of the external magnetic field and the internal current and magnetic field of the electromagnetic gun on the armature thrust is studied. In addition, by analyzing and simulating the force of the arc, it is revealed how the constant magnetic field affects the force and direction of the muzzle arc. With the advancement of superconducting technology, this study provides new ideas for optimizing the performance of electromagnetic railguns.

articleTitle: Research on Different Structures of Additional Rails of Electromagnetic Launch with Rotational Armature
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: High speed rotation of the projectile is one of the most effective ways to improve the firing accuracy of electromagnetic launching process. Asymmetrical structures are adopted to generate the asymmetric magnetic field in this paper. The rotation can be obtained by the electromagnetic torques which are generated by asymmetric magnetic force on the armature. The magnitude of torque can be controlled by the current passing through the additional rails. The finite element dynamics simulation model is built with COMSOL. The motion characteristics of the rotational armature are studied with different vertical distances and cross-sectional shapes of additional rails. The vertical distances of the additional rail are considered as the independent variable, with a variable range from 38 to 50 mm. The maximum rotational speed of the armature is about 169,439 rad/s when the vertical distance is set at 38 mm. The effect of launch velocity and rotational speed of the armature is also discussed with different cross-sectional shapes of additional rails. The cross-sectional area of additional rails is kept constant. The velocity of the armature is unchanged, but the rotational speed of the armature is observed a certain decrease with convex and concave additional rails.

articleTitle: Optimization Analysis of the Bore Cross-Section in Launchers Based on Shooting Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In the electromagnetic launching process, the shooting accuracy at the moment of the armature separating from the launcher is a crucial metric for electromagnetic railgun weapon systems, playing a decisive role in damaging the target. The paper analyzes the manufacturing accuracy of rectangular and anti-arc inner bores on the shooting accuracy of electromagnetic launch weapons under the same other firing conditions. The research shows that, the shooting accuracy of the armature at the outlet is better in the inner bore of the anti arc section than in the rectangular section. The assembly clearance between the armature and the rail on shooting error is much greater than the shooting error caused by the straightness of the launcher bore has a much greater impact on the firing error than the straightness of the launcher inner bore, which can provide technical support for improving the shooting accuracy of the weapon system in the future.

articleTitle: A Calculation method of deposition layer based on armature melting morphology
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The key assumption of this article is that the liquid metal generated by armature melting will rapidly deposit on the rail surface [1]. Combining the calculation method for armature melting morphology [2], this paper introduces a calculation method for determining the distribution of the deposition layer on the rail surface. The evolution law of the deposition layer distribution on the rail surface was obtained by 49 launch experiments. Additionally, the distribution of the deposition layer was calculated based on the launch conditions. Compared with experiments results about the deposition layer from perspectives of distribution trend and thickness, the calculation results was verified. Analysis of deposition layers in the launch direction and vertical direction relative to the insulator during multiple launches reveals that areas with thicker deposition layers carry more current, leading the armature to melt more easily under the influence of Joule heating. Consequently, during multiple launches, the concentration of the deposition layer tends to increase, leading to a thicker layer overall. This ultimately results in significant alterations to the shape of the inner chamber.

articleTitle: General Description of Solid Armatures in Electromagnetic Railguns
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Armature, as an important part of the electromagnetic launch system, is a current carrier which converts electric energy into kinetic energy of projectiles, and it often suffers extreme environment in the launch process. Therefore, the performance of launch system is directly affected by the armature whose structure is the fundamental of the application of launch technology. Among various armature types, solid armatures are the most widely used because of some characteristics of them, like high efficiency and low mass. Based on some key functions of solid armatures, three kinds of requirements including current-carrying capacity, mechanical pressure and electromagnetic contact pressure are proposed in this paper. Besides, research progress of material and structure of the solid armature and its optimization is also introduced in this paper.

articleTitle: A circuitry solution for fast transformer-coupled LC inversion generators
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A circuitry solution for the transformer-coupled LC inversion generator (TCLCG) is presented, which enables a dramatic reduction in the rise time of the generator output voltage.In principle, each TCLCG consists of two storage capacitors and one in-phase 1:1 transformer per stage and one closing switch independently of the number of stages. First, the two capacitors in each stage are charged antiparallel via the primary side of the corresponding transformer. Closing the switch generates two LC oscillating circuits. Whereas the odd-numbered capacitor discharges slowly through the primary inductance of the transformer, the even-numbered capacitor discharges rapidly via the leakage inductance of the transformer and, thus, leads to voltage multiplication due to inversion.The solution discussed here is based on a decisive modification of the previously developed alternative circuitry for the TCLCG. It is shown that the even-numbered capacitors C2n in the TCLCG circuit can be completely removed without negatively influencing the voltage multiplication principle of the TCLCG. It drastically increases the oscillation frequencies f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</inf> ~ (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TL,n</inf>⋅ C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">par</inf>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1/2</sup>, which are given by the leakage inductance of the transformers L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TL,n</inf> and remaining parasitic capacitances C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">par</inf>, typically only some tens of picofarads, due to the structural layout of the generator.Three types of TCLCGs with the modified alternative circuit topology have been set up and successfully tested. All used Ferroxcube 4C65 ferrite toroids for the transformers and a high-pressure spark gap as closing switch.An ultra-compact 4-stage nano TCLCG achieved a record fast rise time of about 10 ns at a peak output voltage of 37 kV and a peak-to-peak voltage of 75 kV in average. A 4-stage micro TCLCG was only marginally slower with a rise time of 15 ns, but already reached a peak voltage of 52 kV and a peak-to-peak voltage of 101 kV in average.A 4-stage high-energy TCLCG with the modified alternative circuitry outperformed a comparative version with the alternative topology, in every respect. Despite a higher storage capacitance of 32.20 nF, instead of 25.12 nF, the generator efficiency went up by 21 percentage points. The generator reached an average efficiency of 53.8% at a charging voltage of 27.0 kV, which corresponds to a gain of 4.30 and a peak output voltage of 116 kV. The average peak-to-peak voltage was 206 kV. The most impressive result is the speeding-up of the generator output rise time by a factor of four from 80 ns for the comparative version with the alternative circuit topology to 20 ns for the version with the new modified alternative circuit topology.

articleTitle: Research on pulsed power supply sequence solution strategy based on charge equivalent
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Whether the discharge current waveform of the pulsed power supply meets the requirements of the load application is an important criterion for evaluating the performance of the pulsed power system. For some applications that require high-power and stable discharge current, finding a fast solution method for discharge sequence and obtaining a reasonable triggering sequence is the key direction of pulsed power supply research [1]-[3]. This paper proposes a sequence solution strategy based on charge equivalent. Firstly, based on the principle of equal charge amounts during the discharge process, the relationship between the current waveform and the number of discharge modules at different stages of discharge is obtained. Secondly, based on the principle that the product of the discharge current and discharge time is equivalent to the amount of charge, the discharge current waveform of each pulsed power supply module is arranged in an orderly manner according to the total discharge current waveform requirements, so as to obtain accurate triggering sequence. Finally, simulation is used to verify the above strategy. The results show that the triggering sequence obtained by the control strategy can make the discharge current meet the requirements and improve the solution efficiency.

articleTitle: Impedance of Plasma Erosion Opening Switch in Particle-In-Cell Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Inductive energy storage is superior in energy density compared to capacitive energy storage, but the drawback is the lack of a high-power opening switch. Low power opening action is possible via some semiconductor switch, and has been applied in small caliber railgun with inductive energy storage for rapid firing railgun application, however for high power application, it seems plasma erosion opening switch (PEOS) is still the only possible choice because in such high-power application all materials will tun into plasma. Previous PEOS experimental research used flash board to produce an explosive field emission plasma stream to conduct a current in the space between cathode and anode in a concentric transmission line, and then with the self-magnetic force induced by the current, the plasma is diverted away from the anode thus completes the opening action. We investigate this behavior in a new PEOS design using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. A ring flash board is first ionized by a pulsed high voltage, and as the plasma fly towards the anode, the impedance between anode and cathode changes. When the conduction current increases to certain degree the self-magnetic field should deflect the plasma stream and the opening is observed. The impedance change during this process is a function of the structure, produced plasma density, and current. It seems the larger the conduction current is, the better the PEOS performs, which makes it a suitable candidate for MW class railgun.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Folded Pulse Forming Line Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Pulse Forming Lines (PFL) must be the longer to achieve the larger width of the output pulse. This means the device tends to become larger as the desired pulse width increases. In case of water dielectric, 1.7 meters are required to obtain a pulse width of 100 nanoseconds. In our development, the axial length of the device was shortened to about one-quarter by folding the transmission line several times. The characteristics of this PFL are reported.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Two Types of Spark Gap Switches for Parallel Triggering
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The impedance-matched Marx generator (IMM) can be considered as a hybrid version of the conventional Marx and Linear Transformer Driver (LTD) generators. This proceeding examines the performance and reliability of different spark gap switches, pressurized with dry air, in a single stage of this generator.In this configuration, eight high voltage dual-polarity bricks must be triggered in parallel. Each brick consists in two capacitors charged up to ±100kV, a switch, and a common matched load. Various experiments focusing on key characteristics of the triggering system, including delivered energy, decoupling between switches and the triggering system, pressure within the switches, and the type of switches used have been studied. Here, two configurations are compared: the first employs eight parallel LTD multi-gap switches [1], while the second uses a more conventional setup with a two main gaps design but in a tubular assembly. The effectiveness of both configurations is evaluated based on performance, ease of setup and maintenance in the objective of a large-scale system.

articleTitle: The Impact of Cathode Geometry on Electron Hot Spot Formation and Ion Beam Properties in Pinched-Beam Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Electron and ion dynamics in a cylindrical pinched-beam diode with 1.6 MV, 800 kA, and 50 ns parameters were studied using particle-in-cell simulations to improve ion beam uniformity. In particular, this work explored how annular cathode tip thickness affected electron hot spot formation and the resulting ion beam. Simulations showed reduced electron hot spots and a more uniform ion beam for a 0.5-mm-thick cathode tip compared to a 3-mm-thick cathode tip.

articleTitle: Research on Methods of Decoupling Current and Friction in Electromagnetic Launching
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Electromagnetic rail launch is an effective way to achieve high velocity. Multiple physical fields such as electricity, magnetism, heat and force are coupled during the launching. The wear of the armature is mainly caused by the joule heat generated by current heating and the frictional heat. Electromagnetic force is mainly determined by the magnitude of the current, so joule heat and frictional heat are two factors that are difficult to separate. It means that the proportion of frictional heat and Joule heat to armature wear cannot be distinguished, which has a certain impact on armature design. The electromagnetic launch device includes simple type and augmented type. The inductance gradient of the simple device is about 0.45uH/m, and the inductance gradient of the augmented device is about 0.9uH/m. According to the electromagnetic force formula, it can be inferred that when the same current is passed through, the electromagnetic force acting on the armature in the two types of launchers differs by half. By controlling the magnitude of the current and the mass of the projectile, it is possible to achieve the same amount of electromagnetic force and the same speed curve on both devices, and obtain experimental comparative analysis of the same amount of friction force. Friction and current can be compared and analyzed by this method.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic force of the jumper conductors in augmented special motor
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The augmented special motor can increase the inductance gradient without increasing the current line density, then improve the launch efficiency. As a result, two-turn series-augmented motor is widely used in small caliber special motors. The jumper conductors in the series-augmented motor conduct the current between two turns of rails, and are acted by electromagnetic force that generated by strong magnetic field during the launch process. In order to guarantee its structural strength and electrical contact performance, a large structure and complex fastening measures are usually required, which seriously restricts the miniaturization and engineering application of series-augmented special motors. This article simulates the electromagnetic force acted on the jumper conductors and analyzes its influencing factors. The simulations show that the electromagnetic force acted on the breech jumper conductors is much larger than that on the muzzle jumper conductors, and the eddy effect is the main influencing factor. Considering the influence of eddy effect, the structure of the jumper conductor should be designed reasonably to avoid larger electromagnetic force, so that compact structure can be complemented.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy of Cascaded Constant Current Charging Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The cascaded circuit topology of charging power supply for pulse capacitor is a new type of charging circuit topology for pulse capacitor, which is especially suitable for megawatt output power of single machine. Based on the topology of cascaded pulse capacitor charging power supply and multi-carrier modulation technology, this paper proposes the carrier phase shifting sum carrier disposition composite control strategy. On the basis of realizing the automatic current closed-loop and improving the load adaptability of the power supply, it further solves the problems of large charging current ripple and large switching loss. Finally, a simulation model of the charging power supply is built in Simulink environment. The simulation results verify the feasibility of the control strategy. When the inductance, switching frequency, input voltage and other conditions are determined, the ripple coefficient is only 4.23%, which effectively reduces the current stress of the power switch device.

articleTitle: Study on Arcing Dynamics and Arc Igniter Design for Railguns
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In the energy recovery methods of electromagnetic railguns, the arc starter is currently the preferred device. However, the high-temperature, high-speed, and high-voltage arc generated by the arc starter has a negative impact on the muzzle and bore of the railgun, and also affects the firing circuit. To gain a deeper understanding of this issue, this article models the arc initiation device and studies its impact on arc evolution. Based on the finite volume method, an arc magnetohydrodynamic model was constructed. A three-dimensional multi-physics field coupling model of pivot rail-arc-muzzle flow field was established through dynamic grid and dynamic material methods. On this basis, the arc morphology and evolution under different emission energy levels and arc initiation device structures were studied. To conduct empirical research, different structures of arc ignition devices were designed using copper tungsten alloy and installed at different muzzle positions for firing tests. The results show that the position, angle, and shape of the ignition device relative to the muzzle have a significant impact on the arc and its evolution at the end of the launch. The research results indicate that by designing the arc ignition device reasonably, the high-temperature arc backflow and erosion can be effectively reduced, and the muzzle flow field environment can be improved. This study has certain reference value for improving the service performance of arc ignition devices, extending orbital life, and enhancing the stability of launch components exiting the chamber.

articleTitle: Monolithic Radial Transmission Line Circuit Modelling Using a 2D Mesh
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The monolithic radial transmission line is a core component of multiple proposed pulsed power machine concepts. It is useful to have a model of this component that captures signal propagation in both radial and azimuthal directions, yet is also computationally lightweight and suitable for use in parameter studies and system-wide optimization. Here we present a circuit mesh approach to modelling this transmission line in two dimensions, and compare the predictions of the model to a 3D finite element electromagnetic model to evaluate its performance in two test cases.

articleTitle: Application of pulsed discharge to separate CFRP layer from CFRP/Steel laminates
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) / metal laminated plate is a promising material for automobiles to contribute to fuel efficiency improvements by weight reduction [1]. However, the dismantling of CFRP-metal bonds has been challenging by hand dismantling, and technology for separating CFRP from metal is required to promote resource circulation. In this study, we evaluated the applicability of pulsed discharge to separate the CFRP layer from the CFRP-Steel laminates and reveal the separation mechanism. From results of analyses, it can be claimed that the vaporization of steel plate and CFRP by the pulsed discharge is a significant factor for the delamination of the sample. Thus, pulsed discharge is effective for separating the CFRP layer from the CFRP / Steel laminates.

articleTitle: Studies of the interaction of the high-power sub-nanosecond pulse with neutral gases
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Pressure ionization threshold of the high-power microwave pulse (~ 250 – 300 MW) for air, He, Ar and SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gases has been defined in the range of pressure ~30 – 170 kPa. articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Model Based Control of a Nonlinear Aircraft Arresting System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This paper presents a model-based robust controller and a subscale experimental demonstration for a subscale motor driven aircraft carrier arresting system. Sensors in the system are limited with no sensors on the aircraft being controlled. The uncertainty in the aircraft’s orientation and position, the long mechanical linkages, along with the nonlinear dynamics and limited sensors, result in control design challenges. The control method is based on an adaptive linear quadratic Gaussian/loop transfer recovery control algorithm that regulates >10 MJ of pulsed energy with MW power transients. The design method generates a controller with good tracking performance for the aircraft position and velocity and successfully arrests the aircraft within cable tension bounds.

articleTitle: Flexible, solid-state, nanosecond pulsed power and the influence of a time-varying plasma load
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: We used our recently developed Solid-State Impedance-Matched Marx Generator (IMG) to generate Plasma-Activated Water (PAW). In this work, we compare three methods to connect the IMG to the PAW-reactor: A direct connection, a 1-m cable, and a 16-m cable. The direct connection and 1-m cable cause pulse elongation, which could be compensated using a parallel resistive load. The 16-m cable preserves the pulse shape, but introduces extra voltage pulses on the reactor from reflections.With the 16-m and 1-m cable we perform various plasma experiments to find the influence of the pulse shape on PAW species production.

articleTitle: Pulse Transformer Investigation Based on an Inductive Toroidal Coil with Coupled Coil Sections
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A toroidal coil was used to set-up a simple experimental pulse transformer (PT) topology with high power semiconductors as opening switches. A load current of more than 8 kA was generated by a primary current of 1 kA. The limiting factor is the voltage at the IGCT switch during turn-off.

articleTitle: Pulse Generator for Impact Ionization Triggering in Thyristors
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Fast HV generators are widely used in many industrial and scientific applications including particle accelerators. Historically, the dominant switching components for beam transfer at CERN were thyratrons with all associated complex triggering/biasing/heating recently joined by the risk of approaching obsolescence. Based on recent communications there is a promising alternative based on standard industrial thyristors triggered by an Impact Ionization (II) process. The main challenge is the need of fast pulse generator with high output voltage with ultra-fast slew rate > 1kV/ns. Due to parasitic capacitance of the thyristors (~100’s of pF), the generator must provide current necessary to charge this parasitic capacitance with kV/ns slew rate. We propose a generator based on ultra-boosted HV SiC MOS transistors followed by a fast Marx generator with small thyristors triggered in II mode. We apply up to > 600V of gate boosting overvoltage to accelerate SiC MOS commutation time by a factor of up to 36 compared datasheet. We such achieved sub-ns switching on 1.7 kV rated SiC MOS generating > 1.3 kV pulse with > 2.2 kV/ns slew rate which is used to trigger II process in thyristor switches in the MARX generator further amplifying output voltage and its slew rate. Our solution is using cheap COTS components and provide promising preliminary results with > 11 kV peak voltage and > 30 kV/ns slew rate.

articleTitle: Fundamental longitudinal electromagnetic (EM) force investigation using DC current
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The purpose of this work was to investigate historical claims of the existence of a longitudinal EM force component acting on metallic atomic current elements in a direction parallel to the current flowing through them. This lies outside conventional textbook physics predictions, yet its existence has been indicated previously and if eventually confirmed will have a significant effect on all technological applications involving high current density (>10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The experiment described here (CRE-Coaxial Recoil Experiment) was able to limit all measured forces to the direction of interest, parallel to the current. The multiple phases of the experiment allowed it to distinguish between the EM and mechanical forces acting on a mobile test armature. All the analyzed experimental data related the force on the armature to the current flowing through the circuit. Modifications were made to the length and location of the armature as well as alterations to the liquid metal containment. Raw and processed results are presented, and a significant amount of analysis was performed to discriminate between the axial mechanical contact forces and any possible longitudinal EM force. The original EM force law, proposed in 1822 by Ampère, includes a longitudinal component and has been found to be qualitatively consistent with all experiments to date including these reported findings and is considered a candidate explanatory theory.

articleTitle: Development of a Kicker Power Supply Driving Bump Magnets for the Korea-4GSR Injection System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Prototype kicker power supplies have been designed for the storage ring beam injection of the Korea 4th generation storage ring (Korea-4GSR). To keep field balance and synchronized kick of the beam, the kicker power supplies drive four kicker magnets. The pulsed magnetic field of kickers should be synchronized within a timing jitter of 5 ns and an amplitude difference of ±0.2 percent. In order to fulfil the performance requirements of the kicker power supplies, the pulse-shape matching mechanism among four kickers and handling two kicker magnets by using one kicker power supply as a parallel driver will be adapted to reduce fluctuation of the kick and the trajectory offset. Specifications of the kicker magnet power supply are the pulse width of 5 us, 200 ns flattop width, a half-sinusoidal waveform with the peak current of 5 kA, and 2 Hz repetition rate. In this paper, the circuitry applied to the design of the power supply and circuit configuration will be discussed.

articleTitle: Influences of Explosive Field Emission Threshold to the Performance of Magnetron with Diffraction Output
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Explosive field emission model is frequently used in particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation of high-power microwave devices, and a common criterion for judging whether the model produces reasonable results is to compare generated explosive field emitted current density with known cathode substance. However, the effects of parameter settings in explosive field emission model go beyond current density because of the complicated nonlinear interactions of produced electron beam with the resonant structures, therefore it is not straight forward to understand the influences of the settings in explosive field emission model. The explosive field emission model contains three parameters: rise time, threshold field, and residual field. In this article we investigate the effects of the threshold field when used in a magnetron with diffraction output (MDO) simulation with 500 kV, 10 ns rise and 10 ns fall time, 100 ns pulse width applied high voltage pulse and compare results of different explosive field emission threshold fields. Preliminary results indicate a higher explosive field emission threshold reduces produced field emission current, but the resultant output power is not proportionally reduced.

articleTitle: Pulse Breakdown of Overvolted Gaps Filled with CO2
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Strong demand for low environmental impact fluids in high voltage power and pulsed power systems drives research in the field of breakdown and recovery properties of common gases such as air, nitrogen, carbon dioxide and their mixtures. Although the dielectric characteristics of these gases have been studied for many decades, their impulsive breakdown properties in overvolted gaps and in strongly non-uniform fields are not fully understood. This work is aimed at the study of the breakdown properties of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in divergent electric field under impulsive stress. Breakdown voltage, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">br</inf>, and time to breakdown, t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">br</inf>, have been measured in an overvolted gap stressed with sub-microsecond positive high voltage impulses with a nominal rate of voltage rise of (1.2-1.4) kV/ns. The gas pressure was in the range from atmospheric pressure up to 5-bar (gauge). The reduced breakdown field, E/N, where N is the gas number density, and E is the field at the tip of the needle electrode have been obtained using an electrostatic model. The scaling relationships i.e. the functional relationships between E/N and Nt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">br</inf> and Nd, have been obtained and compared with data from the literature for lower values of E/N.

articleTitle: Analysis of Contact Pressure Between Armature and Rails of Electromagnetic Railgun
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Armature is an important part of the electromagnetic railgun system. It is connected with two rails to form a loop, thus accelerating the projectile to high speed under Lorentz force. With numerous excellent characteristics, C-type solid armature has become the commonly used type in the research of solid armature electromagnetic railgun. For this armature, an important factor needs to be considered in the launch process, that is, the maintenance of the armature-rail contact pressure. If the pressure is in the proper range, smooth transfer of current can be realized and the transition can be avoided to a certain extent. Based on the contact pressure requirement at the initial stage, intermediate stage and muzzle stage, this paper uses the "10N/kA" empirical formula to model and analyze the armature-rail contact force during the launch by combining simulation and test, thus preventing ablation effectively. The results of this study are great significance to the design of armature and rail structure of the electromagnetic railgun.

articleTitle: Semi-analytical calculation method for eddy current and electromagnetic force in inductors of PPS system
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The electromagnetic force inside the pulse inductor affects the safe operation of the pulsed power supply (PPS) system. The calculation speed of the existing numerical method is too slow for large-scale optimization. This article proposed a semi-analytical method that can realize the fast calculation. This method is based on the discretization and normalization of the coils. The comparison with the simulation verifies the accuracy and rapidity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High Speed, Low Loss and Energy Recovery in Pulsed Power Circuit Using Ultra-High Voltage SiC Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Ultra-high voltage SiC devices were used as the switching device in pulsed power circuits. It is hard to realize both high breakdown voltage and fast switching. Because switching losses increase as di/dt increases. Magnetic assist could be used for lower losses, higher speeds. The switching losses were successfully reduced from 4.57 mJ to 0.41 mJ and the D-S voltage fall time from 151 ns to 66.1 ns at 5 kV charging. In addition, by using six MOSFETs in parallel, the di/dt per element was suppressed and the charge voltage was successfully raised to 12kV. (Switching losses of 8.39 mJ for an input energy of 432 mJ) Also, energy recovery voltage of 3 kV was successfully realized in a 5 kV charge by using an SBD as a reverse current bypass circuit. We developed a switching module using 6 parallel SiC-MOSFETs and applied it to the pulsed power generator with Magnetic assist. The switching loss was 8.39mJ at a switching voltage of 12 kV (input energy=432mJ)

articleTitle: Computational models of Albers and Bragg, 2 MV, 700 kA Pulsed Power Machines with Plasma Filled Rod Pinch Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Albers and Bragg are two flash x-ray sources with Marx generators, Pulse Forming Lines, Magnetically Insulated Transmission Lines and Plasma Filled Rod Pinch Diodes. To support design and stewardship AWE has developed a suite of calculational models, including a circuit model of the electrical system, a 3D electromagnetic model of the multi-channelling oil switch, Particle in Cell models of the Magnetically Insulated Transmission Line, MagnetoHydroDynamic models of the diode, and Monte-Carlo simulations of the flash x-ray source. The suite of models is compared with test results and provides enhanced understanding of the physical processes, a method for gauging operational flexibility and predictions for optimised performance.

articleTitle: Study on breakdown voltage and damage mechanism of an extrinsic V-doped SiC lateral photoconductive device
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This paper investigates the breakdown voltage and damage mechanism of lateral SiC photoconductive devices under extrinsic triggering for high-frequency applications. A lateral device with an electrode spacing of 1mm was triggered by a 1064 nm laser with an 8 ns pulse width under DC voltage. The back-triggered device output 71.3 A at 20 kV, with a power capacity of 275 kW. The power capacity and photoelectric efficiency of the back-triggered device were significantly higher than those of the front-triggered device. The photoelectric efficiency and internal electric field of the device were analyzed by dynamic numerical simulations. The main reason for device damage was that the peak electric field near the anode was close to the theoretical breakdown electric field, leading to partial discharge and breakdown. The reasons for the different electric fields between the anode and cathode were also analyzed.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Improved Topology of Air-core Pulsed Alternator Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The key characteristics of air-core pulsed alternator power systems, namely low impedance, high power density, and high energy storage density, make them one of the optimal choice for direct-drive applications in electromagnetic railguns. These systems deliver several mega-amperes (MA) of current by running multiple pulsed power supplies in parallel, reducing the load on each module. However, this parallel operation lowers equivalent inductance at the end of discharge, compared to the railgun load, which may cause the switch to fail to turn off in a single cycle, leading to excess current stress and increased thermal losses. To address these challenges, the introduction of two new submodules—a discharge protection module and a fast demagnetization module—is proposed. These modules aim to ensure the stable switch-off of the discharge rectifier module and reduce muzzle current, considering the impact of various parameters on system performance.

articleTitle: Study on Influence Characteristics of Sliding Contact of Armature inside the Spatial Curved rails in Electromagnetic Launch
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In the practical application of EMR, the support mode of overhanging beam is mostly used to meet the tactical requirement of azimuth pitch. However, under the condition of the self-weight of the launcher, there must be self-weight curved, as well as the straightness deviation generated in the processing, assembly, manufacturing and molding of tube, forming a non-ideal spatial-curved armature-rail contact interface. In this paper, based on the previous analysis of the armature-rail contact characteristics of horizontal curved and vertical cured, the space cured characteristic model of electromagnetic emission was constructed, and the characteristics of the comprehensive influencing parameters of armature-rail contact were studied by analyzing the input parameters including the space cured, and the output parameters including the mass and velocity of the armature. The research can be used to guide the axial stiffness design of the launcher in the practical application of electromagnetic launch, and to perfect the theoretical research of the non-ideal armature-rail contact interface.

articleTitle: Study on self-breakdown voltage characteristics of gap switches
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Although semiconductor switches are widely used these days, gap switches are still often used in the field of pulsed power that handles high voltage and high current. Although gap switches are simple in structure and can realize high-voltage, high-current switching, they are subject to many uncertainties, such as self-breakdown voltage. In this study, the characteristics of self-breakdown voltage of gap switches are investigated focusing on the flowing current and the filling air pressure between gap switches, and the results are discussed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Supercapacitors as Energy Source for Compact Inductive Pulsed-Power Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: An intermediate energy storage with a high-power density is essential to achieve a compact inductive pulsed power supply for railguns. Supercapacitors promise high power density at a modest energy density, bridging the gap between high-energy lithium batteries and high-power film capacitors. However, they are still considered a new technology mainly utilized in commercial applications including energy recovery systems and hybrid or fully electric vehicles. For these markets, they pose a high interest by providing drastically increased charging and discharging rates and still retain great cyclic life compared to most lithium-ion-based batteries.

articleTitle: Research on Output Voltage Maintenance Control Strategy for Battery Cascade Charging Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The increasing demand for system energy density in electromagnetic launch devices has led to the widespread application of high specific energy capacitors in pulsed power supplies. However, the high leakage current of the high specific energy capacitors will affect the discharge accuracy of pulsed power supplies. Therefore, the charging power supply is required to continuously provide energy to the capacitors to maintain their voltage. Battery cascade charging power supply has gradually replaced high-frequency and high-voltage charging power supply in the field of electromagnetic emission with its advantages of high current and fast charging. However, its circuit topology and working principle lead to significant fluctuations in its charging current, which is not conducive to high-precision control of charging voltage and voltage maintenance. In response to this practical problem that needs to be solved urgently, this article briefly describes the reasons for the voltage drop of high specific energy capacitors. Combined with the experimental data, the equivalent circuit model under voltage drop state was obtained. Then, the model was combined with the circuit topology of the battery cascade charging power supply to establish a simulation platform including the capacitor self-discharge process. Based on this simulation platform, control strategies for maintaining the output voltage of battery cascaded charging power supply are proposed. The strategies use voltage-type control and hysteresis control as specific implementation methods to maintain the capacitor charging voltage. To verify the effectiveness of the voltage maintenance control strategy, a low-power prototype experimental platform with self-discharge characteristic load was build, which the voltage maintenance control strategy was provided by the existing battery cascade charging power supply controller. The experimental results show that the control strategy can effectively maintain the capacitor voltage within the set range, achieving precise control of the capacitor charging voltage.

articleTitle: Study of Solid-State Modulator Topology for Magnetrons
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A magnetron modulator is one of the key components of an electron linear accelerator (linac) system for industrial and medical applications. We developed two types of reliable solid-state modulators: a pulsed transformer driven by IGBTs and a MARX using SiC-MOSFETs. In this study, features and suitable applications of these topologies are investigated.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Research of Ultra-High-Speed Electromagnetic Rail Launch Device
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Electromagnetic rail launch (EML) technology boasts advantages like ultra-high initial velocity, long firing range, controllable overload, and high safety, offering broad application prospects. This paper addresses the research needs of rail damage mechanisms and ultra-high-speed launch technology to design an experimental EML device, establish a circuit model, and perform simulation calculations. Detailed designs were developed for the launching device, armature, pulse power supply, etc., resulting in a large-caliber electromagnetic rail launch experimental system.

articleTitle: The effect of thickness of cathode active material layer on separation of cathode materials in Lithium-ion batteries using electrical pulsed discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The demand of lithium-ion batteries (LiBs) is increasing due to the widespread use of electric vehicles. The technology to separate and recover critical metals contained in the positive electrode active material (PEAM) from spent-LiBs is necessary. In the previous study, PEAM layer was separated from the cathode sheet by Joule heating using pulsed discharge. The object of this study is to clarify the effect of thickness of active material layer on separation of positive electrode in LiBs using the pulsed discharge. When the pulsed discharge was conducted in the conditions with a capacitance of 6.4 µF and charging voltage of 10.6 kV, the cathodes with PEAM layers that thickness of 40 and 60 µm were separated. The cathode with PEAM layer of 25 µm thickness was not separated in the conditions. The simulation results suggested that the thermal stress induced by the temperature distribution inside PEAM layer caused the separation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis of an Axial Flux Air-Core Compulsator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In this contribution, the performance of an axial flux air-core pulsed alternator is investigated. In particular, the numerical analysis of the device is carried out using a research numerical code based on an integral formulation able to consider all the principal electromechanical quantities and phenomena. The considered device is an axial flux four-phase, eight-pole air-core compulsator excited by permanent magnets. The compensation is obtained with continuous aluminum shields attached to the rotors and facing the armature windings.

articleTitle: Standard PEF Equipment for Increasing the Added Value of the Technology in Olive Oil & Wine Industries
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In this work, the use of the same PEF equipment, - the pulse generator and continuous treatment chamber - in both olive oil mills and wineries is discussed, given the increase in added value of the technology in these industries.

articleTitle: The study of dynamic inductance gradient in EM railgun launchers
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for calculating the electromagnetic inductance gradient based on the combination of multiphysics simulation and algebraic computation, and calculates the inductance gradient based on actual launch data. The results indicate that the inductance gradient is not a constant but a curve that varies with time. In this paper’s example, the inductance gradient initially rises rapidly and then decrease slowly. The reasons for these changes are the results of a combination of various factors, such as the variation in different frequency components of the current, changes in the current density distribution caused by the skin effect at different speeds, and so on. The dynamic inductance gradient calculation method presented in this paper provides a more accurate computational means for the study of inductance gradients in EM railgun launchers.

articleTitle: Development of compact Marx generator based on gas discharge tubes (GDTs) for pulsed power experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A compact, triggered Marx generator is developed based on gas discharge tubes (GDTs). This workout presents the life rating of GDT, the output characteristics of the Marx generator, and the design of the triggered Marx generator that mixes solid-state switch and GDTs for triggering.

articleTitle: Nanosecond intense relativistic electron beam propagation in gas and preformed plasma
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: An experimental and numerical study on the propagation of a typical flash radiography electron beam in a gas and a preformed plasma is presented. Simulations are carried out using a full kinetic description with a Particle-In-Cell / Monte-Carlo code in order to interpret experimental results. The simulations show the major role of plasma ion redistribution by the beam space charge during its propagation.

articleTitle: Numerical study of current density on armature and rail interface with dynamic contact
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The electrical contact between the armature and rail is acknowledged as an imperfect electrical contact (ImPEC), exhibiting properties distinct from the bulk. It is necessary to understand the current distribution for future structure design and optimization. This paper proposes ImPEC boundary conditions by combining the contact layer model (CLM) and the Cooper-Mikic-Yoranovich model (CMYM), and the current distribution is numerically studied. The contact pressure and area vary with the input current, sharing similar trends, which show a rapid increase in the contact pressure and area during the current ramp-up stage, being constant in the flat stage, and a gradual decline in the current ramp-down stage. The current is re-distributed with the contact area, which is concluded as forced shifts of current caused by dynamic contact.

articleTitle: Effect of surface morphology on armature melt wear
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Armature melting during electromagnetic launch affects the electrical contact characteristics between armature and rail, which in turn affects the launching process and the service life of the launcher. A coupled multi-physics field model considering rough surfaces is constructed. Based on this, the influence law on armature erosion characteristics is analyzed. the results show that the higher the armature surface characteristic scale factor the lower the overall armature temperature, the later the melting onset time, but the more uneven armature surface melting; the higher the surface fractal dimension the less armature melting. The results provide a reference for the optimization of armature surface processing.

articleTitle: An Improved Gate-Boosting Gate Driver for Ultrafast Switching of GaN Transistors for Nanosecond Pulse Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The fast switching capability of Gallium nitride high-electron-mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) enables the utilization of the GaN transistors in pulsed power generators such as solid-state impedance-matched Marx generator (IMG). In such applications, the faster rise time of the generated high-voltage and high-current pulses enhances the efficiency of plasma generation in the plasma reactor. Additionally, achieving higher switching speeds is possible by utilizing an enhanced gate driver featuring a high driving current capacity and fast rise/fall times. In this article, an improved gate-boosting driving method, originally proposed for IGBTs and then optimized for SiC MOSFETs, has been proposed and implemented for driving 650 V GaN transistors to reduce their turn-on time as effectively as feasible. In the proposed improved gate driver, the switching performance of the main 650 V GaN transistor has been evaluated in both simulation and experiments under pulse operation with a resistive load up to 610 V and 107 A. The obtained rise time results for the proposed gate driver in simulation and experiments are 1.62 ns and 1.71 ns, respectively. Furthermore, current rise rates of ${66.05^{{\text{kA}}}}{/_{{\mu} {\text{s}}}}$ and ${62.39^{{\text{kA}}}}{/_{{\mu} {\text{s}}}}$ achieved in simulation and experiments.

articleTitle: First test results of a 30kA pulsed current generator for a new eddy current septum in the CERN PS extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The presently used direct drive septum magnet (PE.SMH16) deflects protons and ions into the extraction transfer line TT2 from PS ring SS16 towards the experimental areas of the PS complex and the SPS. It has been in operation since 1994 and as a result of an ever-increasing extraction frequency the original average lifetime of 5 years has been reduced to about 2 years. Subsequently it will be replaced with a new and more robust eddy current septum that will require far less maintenance. [1] Together with the new septum a pulsed current generator with 30kA peak current is designed and built. The pulsed current has a flat top that is generated by adding a 2.5kHz fundamental sinewave and a third harmonic with 11% of the amplitude of the fundamental. The flat top amplitude error must be <0.1%. This paper presents first test results of the generator prototype connected to the new magnet prototype by 33m of cable. The pulse generator concept presented here features energy recovery. This concept was chosen because the losses in the load circuit are sufficiently low. The first tests show that we can expect to recover approximately 50% of the energy and thus reducing the energy cost. The design of an energy recovery circuit presents several design challenges resulting from turn-on and -off behavior of GTO thyristors and power diodes. The main current pulse of 200μs length flows through the GTOs. This is followed by an energy recovery current pulse flowing in reverse direction through the magnet and freewheeling diodes. At the end of the energy recovery the current flow must be stopped safely. Diodes with fast reverse recovery are used and GTO dv/dt limitations must be respected. Snubber circuits are placed in the circuit to absorb energy transients. There are three critical phases during the current pulse: GTO turn on, commutation of current from GTO to diode, diode turn off at end of pulse. Measurement results are presented and discussed. Gate drive requirements for safe operation of the GTOs are described and test results are presented. A flat top di/dt error correction is described.

articleTitle: A Numerical Model of Magneto-Electro-Thermo-Mechanical Characteristics at the Armature-Rail Contact Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The movement of the armature during the launch process of the electromagnetic railgun is a type of high-speed sliding electrical contact. The characteristics inside the barrel cannot be measured directly. In this paper, a better prediction numerical model is developed. The model involves mechanical calculation part into previous electromagnetic thermal coupling relationships. Based on the contact pressure between the armature and rail obtained from the mechanical calculation part, as well as the rough surface characteristics, the influence of contact resistance on electromagnetic and temperature distribution is also considered. Finite difference formats of bilinear interpolation characteristic method and exponential high-order compact alternating direction implicit method are used to solve the electromagnetic field distribution and temperature field distribution respectively. Finite element incremental superposition method based on the Updated Lagrangian description is used to solve the stress distribution. The contact interface characteristics of rectangular armature and C-shaped armature without considering contact resistance and considering contact resistance are calculated. Results show that the electromagnetic distribution characteristics of C-shaped armatures are significantly better than those of rectangular armatures.

articleTitle: Transformer-less Driving Circuit for Semiconductor Opening Switch Using Transient Voltage Suppressor Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Solid-state pulsed power generators based on custom fabricated semiconductor opening switches (SOS) produce high-voltage pulses with extremely fast rise times and short durations. It has been demonstrated that off-the-shelf diodes can be operated in the SOS mode by utilizing excitation circuits based on either a bulky saturating pulse transformer or dual DC power supplies. In this paper, a novel alternative, transformer-less, compact, single DC supply driving circuit is presented to drive off-the-shelf diodes into the SOS mode of operation. The proposed circuit consists of a high-pulsed current MOSFET switch, air-core inductors and capacitor. The circuit is used to drive Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) diodes into the SOS mode of operation. As proof of concept, a prototype has been implemented with 22 TVS diodes arranged in two parallel symmetric branches. The obtained results demonstrate that the circuit successfully delivers high-voltage output pulses more than 5.8/4.3kV across a 270Ω/50Ω load with a 6.4ns/6.3ns rise time and FWHM pulse duration of 19.2ns/18.4ns respectively, when excited with approximately 38 mJ source energy. Based on the obtained results, the door is open for future use of off-the-shelf diodes as opening switches in a wide range of solid-state-based pulsed power systems.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Anti-recoil Device for Launcher with Large Recoil Mass
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Orbital launchers have a large recoil mass. In order to maintain its structural stability during the recoil process, the launch system should be uniformly stressed. Based on the characteristics of orbital launcher with large recoil mass, we designed single-cylinder integrated counter-recoils and muzzle brakes which are symmetrical arranged. We built a simple model of the launcher to analyze the force on the recoil part, establish the recoil motion equation, conduct simulation calculations on the recoil elements, and complete the simulation test and assessment of the counter-recoils and muzzle brakes on the impact test bench. We analyzed and compared the simulation data and test data of recoil elements, and the results showed that the hydro-pneumatic counter-recoils and muzzle brakes can provide effective recoil efficiency for orbital launcher with large recoil mass. However, in the application of launchers with large recoil mass, there is a problem of recoil impact in place, and it is necessary to focus on designing the recoil buffer structure.

articleTitle: Pulsed streamer discharges driven by a 500-kV, nanosecond, compact Marx generator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Streamer discharge generation by nanosecond high-voltage pulses in a cylinder-wire reactor is proven as an efficient method for air purification, but a large parametric study on optimizing reactor sizes and voltages over a very wide range of parameters has never been performed. To answer this unresolved question, we aim to generate such discharges at voltages up to 500 kV using a Compact Marx Generator (CMG) with rise times in the order of tens of nanoseconds and pulse widths in order of hundreds of nanoseconds. The resulting discharges are inspected and measured using imaging and electrical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Generation of hydroxyl radicals in atmospheric air under repetitive nanosecond spark discharges
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This experiment investigates the effects of varying the pulse repetition rate of nanosecond plasma discharges on the generation of the hydroxyl radical in atmospheric pressure air. This study enables the analysis of the effects of increased energy injection on hydroxyl yield for air sterilization systems. A custom designed impulse generator was used to generate high voltage impulses with 100s of ns rise times. The presence of hydroxyl was measured using optical emission spectroscopy, with the relative change in measured intensity used to determine increases in the presences of OH• radicals. The resultant measured spectra showed an increase in hydroxyl intensities across the full A-X transitional band with a 3.9 times higher intensity observed in the P1(1) transition (308.12 nm) as a result of 1.6 times increase in power (2 kHz – 14 kHz). further pulse repetition rate increases showed minimal effects.

articleTitle: Energy Characteristics of Transient Spark Discharges in Air
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Transient spark discharges are employed in various practical applications including air-filled plasma closing switches. This work investigates the effects of varying air velocities from 0 to 100 m/s and interelectrode gap distances on energy deposition in transient sparks. A Blumlein pulse generator was used to produce square HV impulsive voltages with magnitude of 20 kV, rise time of 25 ns, rate of rise of 0.9 kV/ns and a pulse duration of 250 ns. These impulses were applied to the needle-needle electrode system resulting in spark breakdown on a rising slope of each HV impulse. The energy deposition into the plasma channel under different air velocities and electrode gaps was obtained through two methods for models of dynamic plasma channel resistance. The results highlight an increase in energy deposited into plasma with an increase in gap length, it was also found that deposited energy marginally changes with an increase in the air velocity.

articleTitle: LResearch on Electromagnetic Launcher Gouging under Non-Ideal Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A model of electromagnetic launcher under non-ideal conditions is established based on the theory of impact dynamics and practical engineering considerations. Numerical simulation is conducted using specialized software to investigate the mechanical properties and gouging characteristics of rail-armature contact during electromagnetic launch under non-ideal conditions. Through numerical computations, distributions of current density, Lorentz force, and stress on the rail/armature interface are obtained. The study explores the gouging characteristics under different conditions, revealing that the non-steady motion of the armature results in high-speed collisions, which are the primary cause of rail gouging. By analyzing the gouging characteristics of electromagnetic launcher under non-ideal conditions, this study provides a basis for further efforts to suppress rail gouging phenomena.

articleTitle: Parameters optimization design of high-speed reluctance coil launchers
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Muzzle speed and efficiency are two important factors that constrain the development of reluctance coil launchers. In order to improve the muzzle speed of the reluctance coil launcher, the number of stages of the launcher is bound to increase, which leads to the complication of the simulation model, long simulation time consuming and low optimisation efficiency. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes a fast optimisation method for high-speed reluctance coil launchers based on genetic algorithm and machine learning. Firstly, based on a 7-stage reluctance coil launcher, determine that the wire diameter and the number of coil layers are the optimization objects; based on machine learning, the wire diameter and the number of coil layers are the optimization objects. Based on machine learning, the fast calculation model is trained with the wire diameter and the number of coil layers as inputs and the muzzle speed as output; the fast calculation model is invoked with the genetic algorithm, and the maximum muzzle speed of the launcher is taken as the fitness function, so as to achieve the fast optimisation of the parameters of the high-speed reluctance coil launcher stage by stage. The results show that after optimisation, an muzzle speed of 113.59m/s can be achieved under the condition of 32-stage launcher with an efficiency of 9.96%.

articleTitle: Lifetime Performance of Pulsed Capacitors under the Combined Effect of Gamma Irradiation and High Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Metalized film capacitors (MFC) are widely used in many fields such as electromagnetic emission. In some irradiated operating scenarios, MFC are inevitably subjected to gamma irradiation, which affects their operational reliability. When a pulsed capacitor is discharged, the discharge circuit will oscillate due to the influence of inductance and resistance in the load. At this time, the capacitor will be affected by the reverse voltage, which seriously affects its lifetime. In this paper, the lifetime performance of metallized polypropylene film capacitors (MPPFC) under different irradiation cumulative doses from 0kGy to 1000kGy is investigated by lifetime experiments with two types of discharge reverse peak factors of 70% and 10%. The experimental results show that the lifetime of MPPFC with two kinds of discharge reverse peak factors have the tendency of increasing and then decreasing, but there is a difference in the trend of the MPPFC lifetime between the two groups of experiments. The theoretical analysis shows that the space charge effect after γ irradiation is the reason for the first increase and then decrease of the MPPFC lifetime, while the difference of the electric field distortion during the discharge process is the reason for the different trends of the MPPFC lifetime at different reverse peak factors after γ irradiation.

articleTitle: Development of Battery Cascade High Voltage Charging Power Supply Based on Time Sequence Encoding
