publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A MW level high-voltage charging power supply suitable for fast and cyclic charging of pulse capacitors is developed to meet the requirements of electromagnetic launch devices. The low-voltage cascade topology is used as the charging circuit, and the control strategy of time sequence encoding is adopted to achieve constant current output. The power supply consists of 16 battery modules, with the peak power 5.5MW, the charging rate 1MW/s, and the ability to cyclic charging for more than 10 times. In addition, a method for eliminating residual voltage of pulse capacitors is proposed, which can convert residual energy into charging energy. The power supply is verified through simulation and experiments, and the results prove that the power supply is effective.

articleTitle: Research on the solution strategy of discharge sequence of pulsed power supply based on reverse fitting of mathematical model
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: With the development of electromagnetic launch technology, the performance requirements of pulsed power supply are becoming higher and higher. To improve the accuracy of the actual output current waveform in the experiment and reduce the cost of experimental testing, establishing an accurate mathematical model and conducting effective simulation to obtain accurate discharge sequence has always been the focus of research on pulsed power supply system. This paper establishes a time domain mathematical model of sequence discharge based on circuit principles and proposes a reverse fitting sequence solution control strategy based on this model. This strategy is based on the current and time equations in each discharge state obtained from the mathematical model. Adopting the principle of maximum current consistency, reverse fitting is performed to find the moment when the pulsed power supply module is incorporated into the loop. Thus, the triggering sequence is obtained. Finally, the results calculated by the mathematical model are compared with the simulation results of the circuit model to verify the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Rotor Strength and Critical Speed of the Air-Core Pulsed Alternator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The Air-Core Pulsed Alternator (APA) is the preferred power supply for electromagnetic launch systems [1]. However, due to the enormous centrifugal force and the electromagnetic impact torque, extremely high demands are placed on the strength of the rotor structure. In addition, the design speed of APA is usually high, requiring the machine to pass through the first-order critical speed rapidly to avoid the occurrence of resonance. This paper investigated the structural strength and critical speed of the rotor, as these are two of the most common issues considered in the structural design of the rotor of APA, and discussed the design of the main dimensions of the rotor on this basis.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Semiconductor Opening Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A system based on inductive energy storage and Semiconductor Opening Switch (SOS) diodes offers a promising solution for the development of nanosecond pulse generators. The SOS effect occurs when a silicon p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-p-n-n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> structure, containing residua] electron-hole plasma after forward pumping, undergoes a current density of more than 1 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> within the reverse pumping. In this study, the numerical simulations of SOS diodes are conducted to gain insights into the dynamics of the SOS effect using Synopsys TCAD. Initially, the accuracy of the model is validated by comparing static voltage breakdown simulations with experimental results. Subsequently, a mixed-mode device with a circuit simulator is utilized to simulate the SOS effect and the processes occurring during the current cut-off stage. This research contributes to advancing the field of pulse power technology by providing valuable insights into the operation of SOS diodes using commercially available software.

articleTitle: Analysis of High Voltage Pulse Characteristics for Electric Weed Control Application
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In this paper, high voltage pulse parameters required for electric weed control are analyzed using current and direct resistance measurement data. In order to do this, prototype of electric weed treatment system is built with maximum voltage/energy of 30kV/4.5J and pulse rate of 1 pulse/s. Measurement data are obtained during treatment of typical European weed plants in the range of voltage/energy levels. Current waveform features that correlate with treatment efficiency are presented. Weed resistance recovery phenomenon is also shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Research on package-level failure of IGBT under pulse conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: At present, the mechanism system of IGBT package-level failure is relatively mature, but there is still a lack of research on this mechanism under pulse conditions. This paper explores the package-level failure of IGBTs under pulse conditions. First, a PCB-based PFN capable of generating hundred-nanosecond pulses was designed, combined with the commonly used drive circuit for IGBT, to measure the collector-emitter voltage waveform and collector current waveform during the turn-on to turn-off process of the IGBT, thereby obtaining the power loss of the IGBT under a single pulse. By using COMSOL software, a 3D model of the IGBT was established, with the power loss of the IGBT as input, to perform multi-physics field coupled simulation, thereby obtaining the temperature distribution and stress distribution of the IGBT, and analyzing the preliminary conclusions of the package-level failure. This study provides guidance for future assessment and prediction of the lifespan of IGBT.

articleTitle: The design of liquid metal current collector in EML
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In electromagnetic launch (EML) system, the base where the rail is located needs to rotate relative to the power source at the bottom and requires an electrical connection. This paper designs a liquid metal-based current collector that meets the above requirements. In the case of a given current and allowing for a 1-degree temperature rise, optimize the volume of the conductive liquid to minimize it, and obtain the corresponding size values of the conductive liquid current collector. The resistance of this current collector, as well as its impact on the load waveform under static conditions, has been measured under the current of 5kA. The experimental results show that the scheme of using conductive liquid as a current collector is feasible.

articleTitle: Effect of Armature Mass on the Efficiency of High Current Linear Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of the high current linear drive system, this paper takes the simple high pulse current linear drive device as the research object, devices the drive system into three parts: power supply system, drive device and armature, and studies the effect of armature mass on the system efficiency. The circuit model of the high current linear drive system and armature motion model are established, and the driving process is simulated based on OrCAD platform. According to the simulation results, the system efficiency can be improved by reducing the armature mass without boundary condition. Under the limit of acceleration boundary, it is necessary to adjust the discharge sequence of pulse power supply system module to adapt to the change of armature mass, and the system efficiency increases first and then decreases with the decrease of armature mass. Therefore, in the case of the same performance of the power system and the drive device, a reasonable design of the armature mass is beneficial to maximize the system efficiency.

articleTitle: Approach Formulation for Frequency Tunability in Gyromagnetic Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Nonlinear gyromagnetic lines are solid-state devices for generating radiofrequency in the GHz range without using vacuum tubes and filament heating systems. These lines have the main applications in platform defense systems in signal jamming for disrupting enemy communications on the battlefield or drone shooting down. Herein, we present a formulation that describes with reasonable accuracy the behavior of the frequency variation when increasing the axial magnetic field or the azimuthal field. Our formulation presents frequency stability with lower values of the axial and azimuthal fields. On the other hand, for higher values of the fields, the formulation presented describes the frequency decrease with the axial field and frequency increase with the azimuthal field, as expected. The experimental results of some papers give evidence of the model's validity.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Trigger Timing for Multi-Stage Coil Launcher
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: To reasonably set the triggering time of each stage coil of the energy recovery type reluctance launcher and improve efficiency, this paper proposes a method based on Bayesian Random Forest Model (BO-RF) and Northern Goshawk Optimization algorithm (NGO) to predict and optimize the on-off timing of IGBT switches in each stage coil. The method was validated by building a simulation model of a 5-stage energy recovery reluctance launcher. The results showed that after optimization, the armature muzzle velocity increased from 71.2m/s to 89.89m/s, and the launcher efficiency increased from 26.78% to 32.86%.

articleTitle: Modelling of vacuum breakdown in the MegaAmpere X-ray Installation (MAXI) output line
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Two MegaAmpere X-ray Installations (MAXIs) have been developed to provide flash X-ray radiographic sources for hydrodynamic experiments. The MAXI generates a power pulse that propagates into a vacuum output line terminating with a diode. The output line is designed to be magnetically insulated and forms a Magnetically Insulated Transmission Line (MITL). During tests with a Large Area Diode (LAD) vacuum breakdown of the output line led to machine downtime. The electromagnetic Particle-In-Cell code Large-Scale Plasma (LSP) [1] has been used to model the MAXI output line to evaluate a hypothesis to explain the cause of the vacuum breakdowns. The model includes possible electrode plasma generation. Modelling results of a failed MITL with electrode plasma generation qualitatively agree with vacuum breakdown measurements. The model indicates plasma filling of the vacuum gap and significant current density increase during the pulse, implying that an arc discharge would have been feasible. Recommendations are made to ensure each output line assembly gives a minimum vacuum gap of (12.5 ± 0.5) mm over a range of azimuthal positions, to use a refined LAD setup for electron energy deposition, and to upgrade this modelling work to the Chicago code [2].

articleTitle: Data driven approach for high-power laser ablation phenomena
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This study introduces a comprehensive data-driven approach to decipher the intricate dynamics of high-power laser ablation phenomena and a vast dataset of experimental observations. Laser ablation experiments were performed using a high repetition rate laser (>1 kHz) or a low repetition rate laser (10 Hz) at a wavelength of 1064 nm. The target sample was an aluminum plate placed on a vacuum chamber. The laser fluence was set to the same value above the ablation threshold. Plasma parameters and laser power were observed by photodiode signals from the orifice probe and laser exit. The drift velocity and ion rectification current were considered a function of laser fluence to confirm the relationship between the plasma parameters.

articleTitle: Impedance Adjustments on a Fast 20kV Solid State Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: A simple way of rapid current pulse generation is to switch a pulse forming line (PFL) onto a resistive load with the same impedance as the PFL. Since switch assemblies become larger with higher voltage requirements, the switch’s geometry can have a significant impact on the pulse propagation properties of the whole circuit. The research in this paper investigates the switch’s propagation characteristics. To test our 20kV solid state switch, we’ve set up a fast PFL circuit for two system impedance situations. In repetitive tests, the switch’s geometrical parameters and numbers of thyristors were changed, to investigate influences on the switching characteristic. The measured results were later used to derive a SPICE model that emulates the switch’s behavior very accurately and takes geometry changes into account. It was found that the rise time is mostly affected by the switch’s distance to its ground plane. The later simulations gave indications that this effect could be caused by the switch’s intrinsic impedance.

articleTitle: Gyrator-Capacitor Circuit Modeling of Tesla Transformer with Partial Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: HEART-50 is a high current electron beam accelerator for high power microwave studies, featuring a low-impedance pulse forming line capable of delivering up to 30 GW to the load. Its coaxial forming line is energized to more than 1 MV by a Tesla transformer, which employs a partial magnetic core configuration to enhance the coupling coefficient while minimizing its weight, volume, and cost [1]. While linear coupling inductances in SPICE circuit simulations have traditionally sufficed for transformer modeling, as model parameters like the coupling coefficient, primary and secondary inductances can be easily measured, discrepancies between simulated and experimental current waveforms arise over extended duration. To address this, we utilize a gyrator-capacitor circuit to emulate the partial magnetic core, with the outer, inner partial cores and the gap represented by different capacitors, and core saturation modeled using the nonlinear capacitors. This approach not only captures the magnetic field paths within the transformer, with the model parameters derived from the physics and geometry of the core rather than relying on black box measurement, but also offers rapid circuit-level simulations, avoiding the time-intensive nature of dynamic 3D transient magnetic field modelling. Prediction from the gyrator-capacitor circuit agree closely with experimental waveforms. Furthermore, this enhanced model provides insights into core saturation dynamics, enabling assessments of transformer performance under high current operation conditions.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation Analysis of Linear Motor Finite Length Transfer Based on Abnormal Armature
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In the engineering process of electromagnetic GUN, traditional transfer methods have complex mechanical problems in the power transmission of abnormal armatures, which cannot achieve safe and convenient transfer with limited travel. In response to this issue, this article adopts the linear motor for research on linear transfer technology. Through analytical derivation, the transmission principle of linear motor in finite length space is elaborated in detail, and a finite element dynamic simulation model of linear motor transfer system is constructed. The model comprehensively considers the coupling effects of structure, electromagnetic and circuit, so as to deeply analyze the performance of the linear motor under different working conditions, including high-precision control of position and torque. The simulation results show that our model can predict the performance of the linear motor transfer system, and provide a platform for improving the performance of machines with different pole-slot combinations and optimizing control performance. Further, this paper serves as a support for relative engineering design and optimization, and a reference for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of Effective Electrode Structure for Metal Removal from Composite Materials Using Pulsed Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The authors investigate the potential of pulsed power technology in recycling of E-waste. Applying the pulsed discharge can separate composite materials into plastic and metal. In this study, pulsed discharge was applied to indium tin oxide (ITO) coated plastic films. We used two electrode types: rod-to-rod electrode and a pair of flat plate electrodes to investigate the effect of electrode structure on the metal removal area in detail. A series of single pulse discharges were applied at various electrode distances. As a result, it was revealed that metal can be removed over a wide range by the pulsed discharge using a pair of flat plate electrodes. When the gap between the electrodes was 30 mm, the removal area by the flat plate electrodes was approximately 3.4 times that by the rod electrodes. Analysis of the current density also revealed that the metal removal area was greatly affected by the current density.

articleTitle: Research Progress on the Characteristics of Repetition-rate Spark Gap Closing Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This paper mainly reviews research progress on the characteristics of repetition-rate spark gap closing switches in IAE, CAEP, including two typical types of switches: (1) passive two-electrode switch and (2) electrically trigged three-electrode switch, which are designed for use in low-inductance, fast-pulse systems (e.g. fast Marx generators) where large peak currents (5~20 kA) and high voltages (20~100 kV) are commuted, and operating repetition rate is no more than 100 Hz. The characteristics of the three-electrode field distortion spark gap switch were studied in detail, including breakdown voltage, time delay and jitter, operation at a high repetition rate, and electrode erosion and service-time, etc. Based on a two-electrode spark gap switch, channel resistance and thermal effect were studied. After 9000 pulses running under the conditions of peak current 14.7 kA and pulse width of 160 ns. The discharge channel of the switch generated about 36.6 kJ of heat, the average resistance of the spark channel was calculated to be about 0.12 Ω through Joule heating effect.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-channel Pulse Signal Generator with Adjustable Time Sequence*
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The development of electromagnetic launch technology imposes higher requirements on the discharge control of Pulse Forming Networks (PFN). This paper introduces a multi-channel time sequence pulse signal generating platform based on FPGA NiosII system. The user logic is designed by employing modular programming methodologies. Furthermore, the host computer software is developed utilizing the Qt Creator to facilitate comprehensive control over 30-channel output pulse signals. Within a short delay range, the adjustment step size of channel output time sequence can reach 20ns. To meet various discharge requirements, the signal generator is designed with the capability to store multiple sets of time sequence data. Upon receiving of a designated group number, it promptly calls the corresponding time sequence to generate trigger pulses, thereby swiftly modulating the output current waveform of the PFN. To verify the correctness of the FPGA logic program, SignalTap II Logic Analyzer, an embedded logic analyzer of the Quartus platform, is used to logically judge the FPGA output signals. Additionally, a digital oscilloscope is employed for precise measurement of analog signals from FPGA pins. The experimental waveforms demonstrate that the FPGA logic program meets the design requirements. The connection between host computer and FPGA is established through serial communication for joint debugging and testing. In order to test the signal generator's adjustment functionality of time sequence, the host computer issues the group number. Test results substantiate that output pulse signals of the signal generator are accordant with the setting of the host computer, and the generator can update the output time sequence online based on the received group number. Applying this signal generator to PFN systems allows flexible adjustment of multi-module trigger time sequence according to discharge waveform requirements, which is beneficial for improving the discharge accuracy of PFN systems and expanding their application environment.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Space Launch - The Economic and Operational Benefits of the Variable-Pitch Screw Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel ground launch assist technology, the Variable-Pitch Screw Launch (VPSL), which utilizes magnetic coupling with variable pitch leadscrews to achieve high exit velocities at significantly reduced costs compared to traditional chemical rockets. VPSL addresses the limitations of current linear accelerators by circumventing the switching constraints of linear motors and eliminating the rail wear commonly associated with railguns.Significantly, the capital cost of VPSL is proportional to the square of the exit velocity (ΔV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), providing a more favorable economic scaling compared to the exponential cost increases (exp(ΔV/V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>)) inherent in chemical propulsion systems and the cubic cost growth (ΔV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) observed in some linear motor components. A parametric model estimates the capital cost of a human-rated launcher capable of accelerating 21,181 kg vehicles to a speed of 11,129 m/s to be 32 billion in 2024 USD.

articleTitle: Pulsed Power Drilling for Deep Secure Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: We are considering pulsed power technology to enable wide meter diameter, 5000-meter-deep drilling for safe and permanent disposal of nuclear waste. The tool will be a drilling tower driven by repetitive pulsed plasma of GW peak power at the mud-rock interfaces of the drilling front. The challenges are efficiency in cost and in energy, a very short duration electric power pulse, and performance at high hydrostatic pressure and elevated temperatures. Projected design goals comprise a bore hole diameter of at least 1m, a drilling speed of 1m per hour, an average power of 100's of kW at the drilling bits and a modular construction

articleTitle: Research on Muzzle Arc in Ultra High Speed Air Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The arcing phenomenon of the muzzle after the armature out of the bore restricts the development of electromagnetic launch technology. Because the physical process of the armature exiting the muzzle is complicated, it is difficult to accurately predict the arc suppression process and arc conduction characteristics of the muzzle. This article researched on the muzzle arc in ultra high speed air flow of electromagnetic launch technology. Numerical analysis of the muzzle arc has been done. Then the magnetohydrodynamic simulation shows that the relationship between muzzle arc and air flow. After that, the experimental results indicate the arc suppression device works, which means that the arc is suppressed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Damage Mechanism of F881 Glass Fiber Epoxy Composites Under Impact Load
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: As the main insulation material of electromagnetic launcher, has long-term electrical-thermal- mechanical multifactor aging effect, and the mechanical impact stress damage is the most serious. Aiming at F881 glass fiber epoxy composite material, a mechanical impact experimental platform was built. The charger was used to charge the 4mF capacitor, and the pulse voltage values were set to 2.0 kV, 2.25 kV and 2.5 kV, respectively. In order to improve the experimental efficiency, two groups of launchers were used in parallel. The impact times were 100 ~ 700 times, 100 ~ 600 times and 50 ~ 400 times, respectively. The peak values of impact stress calculated by simulation are 311.7 MPa, 362.7 MPa and 477.8 MPa respectively. In order to explore the impact damage mechanism of the sample, the micro and macro analysis of the sample was carried out, including scanning electron microscopy, elastic modulus, bending strength, impact strength and Poisson 's ratio. The variation law under different impact loads and times was analyzed, and the failure mechanism was analyzed.

articleTitle: Ultrashort Rise Time Pulses for Air Purification using a Solid-state Impedance-matched Marx Generator with Planar Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In this work a new planar waveguide concept is proposed based on the topology of the solid-state Impedance-matched Marx Generator, using only printed circuit boards as structural components. The topology is designed to generate repetitive high-voltage pulses with ultrashort rise time for the application of large scale efficient air purification. Placing planar waveguides on printed circuit boards results in a high accuracy and low-cost design to achieve the shortest possible rise time out of a Marx generator topology using solid-state power components. Switches based on gallium-nitride are selected to provide substantially shorter Marx stage rise times. A four stage prototype of the topology is developed to verify its operation and to provide measurement data on the ultrafast solid-state Marx system compared to performed 3D electromagnetic simulations. Measurement results on the prototype show rectangular 150 ns pulses above 1.0 kV with rise times below 2.0 ns. The topology can be used on its own or be part of a more complex structure for larger system powers, as the coaxial output is designed for 50 Ω impedance [1].

articleTitle: Research on the Temperature Rise and Cooling Methods of Inductor in Inductive Pulsed Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Repetitive operating frequency is one of the key performance parameters of inductive pulsed power supply (IPPS). Focused on the temperature rise of the pulsed inductor when IPPS works continuously, this paper establishes a multi-physical field-circuit coupling numerical simulation model based on the traditional meat grinder with SECT circuit and the structure of the energy storage inductor, and the "temperature rise - heat dissipation" process of the pulsed inductor is solved. The results show that the temperature of the internal metal part of the inductor rises rapidly during the discharge process, and during the discharge interval the heat slowly diffuses outward, which will obviously accumulate when working frequency becomes high; The increase of temperature will affect the conductivity of metal and change the equivalent resistance, which result in a different working state of the circuit, and the current will be indirectly interfered. The reliability of analysis results is verified by practical discharge experiment. Based on the model, three possible cooling methods were proposed and their cooling effects are preliminarily compared through simulation calculations, which provides the basis for necessity and optimization experience for the practical cooling design of inductors in IPPS.

articleTitle: Development of a Fast-Rising Short-Pulse High-Voltage Power Supply using SiC-MOSFETs for the J-PARC Kicker System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: We have been developing a semiconductor switch power supply using SiC-MOSFETs to replace the conventional thyratron switch power supply. The newly developed power supply outputs a rated output of 40kV/2kA, a pulse width of 1.2μs, and a repetition rate of 25Hz using the LTD circuit system. This power supply has achieved performance that replaces the current kicker power supply at J-PARC. The specifications of the developed LTD pulse power supply circuit for SiC-MOSFETs, the corona-free structure of the constructed high-voltage application section, and the results of power saving and miniaturization will be reported.

articleTitle: Launch Efficiency of Capacitive Energy-Storage Electromagnetic Railgun System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Electromagnetic railgun have high initial velocity, long range and other advantages. Improving the launch efficiency is one of the most important needs for the application of electromagnetic rail launch technology. Based on the subsystem models of pulse power supply, rail and armature of railgun, the equivalent circuit mathematical model of the electromagnetic rail gun system under lumped parameters is established. The effects of capacitance, voltage, inductance, resistance and acceleration distance on the system efficiency were simulated and analyzed. The results of the study are of great significance in guiding the design of the electromagnetic launch system.

articleTitle: Optimizing Control Strategies for High-Power Capacitor Chargers with a SiC-based LC-resonant Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Different control strategies for a SiC-based LC-resonant converter used as a capacitor charger are presented. The best suiting operation mode is selected and a possible way to improve the performance of the selected topology by up to 34 % is presented.

articleTitle: Research on inductance gradient of electromagnetic railgun based on eddy current field analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Inductance gradient has a significant effect on muzzle kinetic energy and launch efficiency in electromagnetic railgun. Inductance gradient is determined by the current distribution in the armature and rail, transient skin effect, velocity skin effect, and proximity effect are the main physical mechanisms affecting the current distribution of electromagnetic railgun. Additionally, the structure and size of the rail also have an impact on current distribution. In order to analyze inductance gradient, the control equation of the electromagnetic railgun is analyzed, and the 3D motion model of the electromagnetic railgun is established. The distribution of the 3D current and magnetic field under the influence of the velocity skin effect is calculated, and then the time-varying curves of the inductance gradient during the whole launch process are drawn, curves show that the inductance gradient trend when velocity skin effect is considered is opposite to that not considered. At the same time, the inductance gradient under different rail structures is compared by simulation calculation, the results show that the inductance gradient of the rectangular rail is larger than that of the T-shaped rail and the arc-shaped rail. Finally, the effect of the dimensions of the rectangular rail on the inductance gradient is investigated, and the results show that the inductance gradient of the rectangular rail decreases gradually with the increase of the rail width, and increases and then decreases with the increase of the rail height.

articleTitle: Influence of arc armature geometric parameters on current distribution at the armature/guideway interface
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: In this paper, a parametric model of arc armature is established. And simulation models considering velocity skinning effect and pre-contact resistance are also established in this paper using COMSOL. Through this model, the effects of each parameter of the armature on the current distribution at the armature-rail interface are investigated, and by processing the results, the effects of different parameters on the current distribution at the armature-rail interface are compared. It is shown that the curvature of the arc surface, the amount of internal retraction and the length of the tailplane have the greatest influence on the current distribution at the armature-rail interface.

articleTitle: Optimising a compact HVPS for electron beam applications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: The Insulated Core Transformer (ICT) technology enables the design of a modular and compact High Voltage Power Supply (HVPS). In this paper, the requirements for a prototype with 120 kV / 100 mA resulting from the application for electron beam technology will be discussed. Galvanically isolated circuits with a high bandwidth of 2.5 Msps are used to measure the current and voltage of the HVPS. Vacuum breakdowns in the electron beam gun result in potential shifts, which pose major challenges for the associated digital measurement and control equipment. Our approach using mostly compact, low cost SMT components is presented.

articleTitle: A combined discrete-continuous model for railgun simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Railgun weapon systems can accelerate projectiles to hypervelocities. Even though they are still at prototype stage, the feasibility of fitting a ship with such weapon system is an ongoing investigation.Given the limited power supply on board of ships, research efforts have been put in maximizing the efficiency of such weapon system against incoming missiles while minimizing the energy consumption.To conduct such optimisation studies, we rely heavily on computer simulated scenarios which are greedy in simulation time. For accurate modeling of parameters’ influence on weapon lethality and energy consumption, it becomes a necessity to simulate the complete projectile path from the acceleration in the railgun to its end of trajectory at target engagement and damage assessment. The nature of the complex physics involved in such simulations requires the modeling of the interaction of processes which can be represented by continuous time and discrete event models.This paper presents a computational framework which models the interaction of the processes during projectile acceleration in the railgun. It is computationally efficient to use a modular event driven environment where the different processes can interact. These processes can then be solved at different time scales with different numerical methods. The models are implemented using ConcurrentSim, which is a discrete event package in Julia that manages the scheduling of the events.The presented model is validated using data from a Distributed-Energy-Supply (DES) railgun. Parameters for a non DES railgun configuration (breech-fed) are then determined to meet the performance of the DES railgun used for validation. The energy supply for both railguns is generated by the discharge of capacitors banks.

articleTitle: Study on the Dynamic Characteristics of Electromagnetic Rail Launcher Considering the Insulating Supports
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: During the discharge of the electromagnetic rail launcher (EMRL), the electromagnetic repulsive force and the armature-rail contact force act on the rail, resulting in complex dynamic response of the rail. In-depth study and analysis of the dynamic response of the launcher can provide theoretical basis for its engineering application. In this paper, a three-dimensional model of EMRL is established, in which the insulating supports are not simplified as previously reported, they are treated as real three-dimensional objects. The results show that the inward deformation of the rail is reduced due to the existence of insulating supports. The smaller the elastic modulus of the insulating supports, the greater the maximum deformation of the rail in the direction of load.

articleTitle: Study on the Testing Methods for Discharge Efficiency of PVDF-based Film Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: Capacitors based on PVDF-based films with high dielectric constants exhibit high energy storage densities and demonstrate significant application potential in the fields of pulsed discharge and high-power charge-discharge. Due to the unique polarization and ferroelectric properties of PVDF-based dielectric films, accurately measuring their discharge performance poses a challenge. Currently, research on the discharge efficiency of PVDF-based film capacitors is limited. This paper focuses on the discharge efficiency of PVDF-based film capacitors and analyzes the discharge efficiency of PVDF-based film capacitors and a control group PP film capacitors using the voltammetric differential method. We have established a relevant test platform that can collect voltage and current data in real-time from the test circuit and perform discharge efficiency tests on capacitors under different voltage conditions. We have also developed a simulation model to compare the discharge behavior under different voltages. The results show that the PP film capacitors are consistent with the simulation results under any discharge voltage, while the PVDF-based film capacitors have a higher degree of consistency with the simulation at low voltages. As the voltage increases, the deviation from the simulation results also increases. By comparing the PP film capacitors with the simulation calculation synchronously, we analyze the discharge capability of the PVDF-based film capacitors, derive the equivalent resistance values under different voltages, and further enrich the testing methods for the discharge capability of this type of capacitor.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a MARX-type Klystron modulator Using Semiconductors for Practical application
publicationTitle: 2024 10th Euro-Asian Pulsed Power Conference, 25th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams and 20th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Launch Technology (EAPPC/BEAMS/EML)
abstract: We have developed a MARX-type klystron modulator using SiC semiconductors. This modulator outputs 145 kV/120 A pulses with its width of 10 us and repetition frequency of 200 Hz. The MARX circuit cuts out pulses of 10 kV/1800 A from the built-in main capacitors, and a transformer boosts it to 145 kV/120 A. In this report, we summarize the results of various measurements, such as pulse flatness and voltage stability, in addition to a result of destructive tests of FETs to guarantee its operation in an event of a load short circuit.
